We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions. The target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

We have applied template 1914393 (which seems to break a C-alkyl halide? Actually it gave precursors: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1 and FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1. That seems to split the side chain with a chloromethyl? Wait original target has Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached to the triazine? Actually the target: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. So there is a phenyl attached via CH2 to the triazine (c2nnn...). The side phenyl has a substituent CN4CC(F)C4 (a fluorinated azetidine? Actually N4CC(F)C4 is a 3-member? It's a N-azetidine with F). The template 1914393 gave a precursor where that side phenyl is replaced with a chlorophenyl? Actually product: FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1. That's a fluorinated azetidine attached to a phenyl with a chlorine substituent. So the template likely is a SN2 substitution: the side chain CH2 attached to phenyl is replaced by Cl? Actually the forward reaction would be SN2: Cl-CH2-Ph + amine -> amine-CH2-Ph? Not sure.

We also applied amide disconnection (647549) to get two fragments: COc1cccc(N)c1 (anisidine) and Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O (a triazine? Actually it's a 1,2,4-triazol-3-yl carboxylic acid?).

But we need 3 steps total. Likely route: 1) Disconnection of amide bond between anisidine and triazine carbonyl. 2) Disconnection of the side chain linking triazine to phenyl (C-alkyl halide SN2). 3) Disconnection of the phenyl substituent to the azetidine (maybe substitution of halide with amine). Could also use Friedel-Crafts acylation for attaching anisidine? But guidance mentions Sn2, Friedel-Crafts acylation, substitution of hydroxyl to halide. We need to incorporate those.

We have three reactions: maybe step1: SN2 to attach phenyl side chain to triazine (break C-CH2 bond). Step2: substitution to convert alcohol to halide on phenyl side chain (maybe convert benzylic alcohol to chloride). Step3: Friedel-Crafts acylation to attach amide to anisole? Actually amide formation is not Friedel-Crafts. Friedel-Crafts acylation introduces acyl onto aromatic ring, breaking halide. Could be used to attach carbonyl onto anisole? The target has anisole ring with amide attached at para position? The anisole ring (COc1cccc(... )c1) has an amide substituent at para? Actually COc1cccc(NC(=O)...)c1: methoxy at position 1, amide at position 5? So could be formed by Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole with acyl chloride derived from triazine? That would give aryl ketone, not amide. So maybe not.

Alternative: Use substitution to convert phenol to halide then SN2 to attach azetidine.

We have precursor from template 1914393: FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1. That's the side chain fragment with a chlorophenyl. So we need to get that from a phenol (maybe via substitution of OH to Cl). So step2: substitution of benzylic alcohol to chloride. Then SN2 attaches to triazine.

Thus route: Target -> break amide -> anisidine + triazine carboxylic acid (or amide precursor). Then break C-CH2 bond between triazine and phenyl side chain via SN2 (retro SN2) giving triazine with H? Actually retro SN2 would give triazine with leaving group (maybe Cl) and phenyl chloride? The applied template gave precursors: anisidine fragment and side chain fragment (FC1CN...). So step1 is amide disconnection. Step2 is SN2 disconnection of side chain: triazine fragment (with maybe H) and side fragment (FC1CN...). Actually the amide fragment we got is COc1cccc(N)c1 (anisidine) and Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O (triazine carboxylic acid). But we need also the side chain attached to triazine: the triazine currently has a substituent Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3. In the amide fragment we got Nc1[nH]nnc1C(=O)O which is just the triazine core with carboxylic acid, no side chain. So we need to further disconnect that side chain from triazine. That would be a SN2 retro: break C-CH2 bond between triazine carbon (maybe at N?) and phenyl. The template 1914393 gave side chain fragment and the rest of molecule (without side chain). The rest is COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1 (i.e., target without side chain). So step2: break side chain off triazine, giving that intermediate (target without side chain) and side fragment FC1CN... So step3: need to get side fragment from simpler precursors via substitution of hydroxyl to halide then SN2? Actually side fragment is FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1. Could be made by substitution of benzylic alcohol to chloride on phenyl, then SN2 with azetidine? The side fragment contains a chlorophenyl attached to azetidine via CH2. So we could propose: start from phenyl with benzylic alcohol (C-CH2-OH) and azetidine with nucleophile (maybe N of azetidine) to do SN2 to form C-N bond, after converting alcohol to chloride. So step3: substitution of benzylic alcohol to chloride (using SOCl2). Then SN2 of azetidine nitrogen onto benzylic chloride to give side fragment.

Thus overall 3 steps: 1) Amide formation (retro) -> anisidine + triazine carboxylic acid. 2) SN2 disconnection of side chain -> intermediate (anisidine + triazine carboxylic acid) + side fragment (azetidine-chlorophenyl). 3) Substitution of benzylic alcohol to chloride (retro) -> phenyl benzylic alcohol + azetidine.

We need to provide JSON with reactions and template IDs. We have template IDs: amide disconnection 647549. SN2 disconnection 1914393. Substitution of hydroxyl to halide? Need a template for converting alcohol to halide. Search for functional_groups_broken: aliphatic hydroxyls.
